findings.key_quote: More Personal Computing revenue decreased driven by Gaming, offset in part by Search and news advertising as well as Windows OEM.
findings.justification: E3 has period_status EXACT_MATCH for the three months ended December 31, 2025. It states that More Personal Computing revenue decreased driven by Gaming. Gaming is part of More Personal Computing segment. A decrease driven by Gaming contradicts the assertion that gaming was a source of strength in Q2 FY2026 (the quarter ended December 31, 2025).

E5 shows Gaming revenue for the three months ended December 31, 2025 was $5,958 million compared to $6,581 million for the three months ended December 31, 2024. This is a decline of $623 million or approximately 9.5%. A revenue decline contradicts the claim that gaming was a source of strength in the quarter ended December 31, 2025.

findings.key_quote: Three Months Ended December 31, 2025 Compared with Three Months Ended December 31, 2024 Research and development expenses increased $587 million or 7% driven by investments in compute capacity and AI talent and impairment charges in our Gaming business.
findings.justification: E4 mentions impairment charges in the Gaming business during the three months ended December 31, 2025. While this is negative context about gaming, impairment charges relate to asset write-downs and do not directly measure whether gaming was a source of strength in terms of revenue or operational performance. This is related context but does not definitively decide the assertion.
